stories.title: Meta to pay $17.1 billion in social media addiction settlement
stories.details: Meta has agreed to a landmark settlement of up to $17.1 billion to resolve claims regarding social media addiction. The case highlights growing legal and societal pressure on tech giants to address the impact of their platforms on users.

stories.title: Anthropic enters physical AI market
stories.details: Anthropic has launched the Model Hardware Standard, a research preview that links large language models like Claude to physical equipment such as robotic arms. This initiative aims to bridge the gap between AI software and real-world industrial hardware.

stories.title: OpenAI and 100+ firms warn of imminent AI cyberattacks
stories.details: A coalition of over 100 companies, including OpenAI, Google, and Microsoft, has issued an open letter warning that AI-powered cyberattacks are becoming more frequent. They are calling for collective action to prioritize security and traceability in AI development.

stories.title: Judge blocks Pentagon's Anthropic ban
stories.details: A federal judge has overturned the Pentagon's decision to blacklist Anthropic as a supply-chain risk. The ruling stated that national security concerns do not grant the government a 'blank check' to retaliate against companies that refuse to support specific military use cases.

stories.title: Meta adds kill switch to smart glasses
stories.details: Meta has patented a 'mute or lock' switch for its Ray-Ban AI glasses to address privacy concerns and misuse. The move follows reports of the device being used inappropriately and public backlash regarding sensor privacy.

stories.title: Nvidia pauses revenue-sharing deals
stories.details: Nvidia has temporarily halted its program providing credit support and revenue sharing to cloud providers building AI data centers. The company is concerned that these aggressive financial arrangements could attract antitrust scrutiny.

stories.title: Flash floods in Nepal leave hundreds dead
stories.details: A devastating flash flood in Nepal and Tibet has resulted in over 500 deaths and 2,000 people missing. Survivors are grieving the loss of relatives and homes as rescue efforts continue amidst fears of further flooding from an overflowing lake.

stories.title: Journalist reports from the Nepal flood zone
stories.details: British reporter David Brown provided a firsthand account from Battar, describing the harrowing experience of evacuating alongside local residents as floodwaters surged. The situation remains critical as international attention focuses on the decimated border region.

stories.title: Political uncertainty as MPs return to Westminster
stories.details: MPs are returning from recess to a new government and an untested prime minister. Political editor Steve Swinford has outlined a 'blizzard of announcements' planned by Downing Street to project a sense of change.

stories.title: Gordon Brown on the future of Northern Ireland
stories.details: Former Prime Minister Gordon Brown has stated his belief that Ireland will eventually be united. He also discussed his vision for a better Britain and his desire to avoid being a 'backseat driver' in current political affairs.

stories.title: Anti-asylum protests in Norfolk
stories.details: A small Norfolk town has been engulfed by anti-asylum protests centered around the RAF Barnham site. The situation highlights the ongoing national tension regarding immigration and asylum policy.

stories.title: Private school fees exceed £70,000
stories.details: For the first time, top private school fees in the UK have surpassed £70,000 per year. This milestone reflects the rising costs of elite education in the country.

stories.title: Tragedy on the Atlantic migration route
stories.details: A harrowing incident occurred where over 200 people set sail for Europe from West Africa, but only 36 survived. The route is currently considered the deadliest in the world for migrants.

stories.title: Russian sanctions fueling Canadian car theft
stories.details: A black market for stolen Canadian cars has emerged, with Russia serving as the primary destination. Smugglers are actively meeting the demand created by international sanctions.

stories.title: US diplomat's controversial style
stories.details: John Coale, a Trump envoy, is facing criticism for his unconventional approach to diplomacy, which involves using vodka and dirty jokes. Critics argue he is conceding too much to authoritarian leaders.

stories.title: Victims condemn glorification of Ratko Mladić
stories.details: Victims of the Bosnian war have condemned the ongoing glorification of convicted war criminal Ratko Mladić. Despite his imprisonment, many continue to view him as a hero.

stories.title: UK petrol prices hit four-year high
stories.details: UK petrol prices have reached their highest level in nearly four years just as the bank holiday getaway begins. The increase is putting pressure on travelers and the broader economy.

stories.title: Federal Reserve focuses on stable prices
stories.details: The chair of the Federal Reserve has reiterated that the central bank's primary mandate is to deliver stable prices. The statement comes as inflation continues to persist in the US economy.
